---
title: "check-wikipedia-further-reading.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, blocking check that flags a Wikipedia citation or link
in a list item of a Further reading section.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-18) is that Wikipedia pages never appear
in Further reading sections: they are citations only.
This implements
[gha#1093](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1093).

The check flags a list item (starting with `-`, `*`, `+` or `1.`)
that contains a `@wikipedia_<key>` citation,
a link or URL to `wikipedia.org`,
or the words `Wikipedia on`,
when the item is in a reading context:

- **A reading heading.**
  The item's nearest preceding heading matches
  *further reading*, *online references*, *going further*,
  *additional reading*, *learn more*, or the word *reading*.
  The match is deliberately broad:
  a heading such as "Reading data into R" opens a reading context too,
  since a section about reading can still hold a reading list.
  Any later heading resets the context.
- **A `.reading` div.**
  The item sits in a `::: {.reading}` div.
- **A reading subfile.**
  The file name contains `further-reading` or `sec-reading`.
  A subfile's heading is in its parent chapter, which the check cannot see,
  so the whole file counts.

The check does not flag a Wikipedia citation in ordinary prose,
a list item outside a reading context,
or anything in a code fence.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported.
The whole file is parsed, because the heading sits far above the item,
and only items with an added line are kept.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.
Every run prints how many lines, files and reading-context list items
it examined.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default               | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd *.md'`        | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`                  | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `true`                | Fail the workflow when Wikipedia is found in Further reading. Set `false` for warnings only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`               | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`              | Python version to set up. |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-wikipedia-further-reading.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a Wikipedia citation (`@wikipedia_<key>`) or link in a
# Further reading list item on lines a PR adds. Wikipedia pages are citations
# only and never belong in Further reading. Blocks by default; ordinary prose
# citations are never flagged.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check Wikipedia in Further reading

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-wikipedia-further-reading.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                    # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                            # warn instead of block (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-wikipedia-further-reading.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-wikipedia-further-reading.yml)
for the full caller stub.
